scenes.title: The Double Wedding at Sparta
scenes.summary: At nightfall Telemachus and Peisistratus reach Lacedaemon and find Menelaus giving a wedding feast for his kinsmen: he is sending his daughter Hermione, promised at Troy, to the son of Achilles in the land of the Myrmidons, and bringing the daughter of Alector from Sparta for Megapenthes, his son by a slave woman. A divine singer sings to the lyre and two tumblers whirl among the guests.

scenes.title: Menelaus Welcomes the Strangers
scenes.summary: Menelaus' attendant Eteoneus asks whether to unyoke the strangers' horses or send them on to another host; Menelaus rebukes him, remembering how often he was a guest himself, and has them brought in. They marvel at the radiance of the house, are bathed, clothed and fed, and Menelaus tells them that they are surely the sons of kings and gives them the chine of honor from his own portion.

scenes.title: The Wealth and Grief of Menelaus
scenes.summary: Telemachus whispers to Peisistratus that the house must be like the court of Olympian Zeus. Menelaus overhears: no mortal can vie with Zeus, but he gathered his wealth in eight years of wandering, to Cyprus, Phoenicia, Egypt, the Ethiopians, the Sidonians, the Erembi and Libya, while his brother was murdered at home. He would give two thirds of it to have back the men who died at Troy, and he mourns above all for Odysseus.

scenes.title: Helen Recognizes Telemachus
scenes.summary: At the name of his father Telemachus weeps behind his purple cloak, and Menelaus ponders whether to question him. Helen comes from her fragrant chamber like Artemis, with her handmaids and the silver work basket given her in Egyptian Thebes, and at once sees in the stranger the likeness of Odysseus' son. Menelaus agrees: such were Odysseus' feet and hands, his glances and his hair.

scenes.title: Tears for the Lost
scenes.summary: Peisistratus confirms that this is Telemachus and explains their coming. Menelaus says that he would have given Odysseus a city in Argos and lived beside him all his days, had a god not begrudged them. All four weep, Peisistratus for his brother Antilochus; he asks that they leave lament until the morning, and Menelaus praises his good sense and Nestor's fortune, and they turn again to supper.

scenes.title: Helen's Drug and the Tales of Troy
scenes.summary: Helen casts into the wine an Egyptian drug that banishes grief, a gift of Polydamna, wife of Thon. She tells how Odysseus slipped into Troy disfigured as a beggar, and how she alone knew him, bathed him and swore to keep his secret. Menelaus tells how she came to the Wooden Horse with Deiphobus and called the chieftains by name in their wives' voices, and Odysseus held back Diomedes, Menelaus and Anticlus until Athena led her away.

scenes.title: Night in Menelaus' House
scenes.summary: Telemachus asks to go to bed; Helen has beds made in the porch, and Menelaus sleeps in the inner room with Helen beside him.

scenes.title: Telemachus States His Errand
scenes.summary: At dawn Menelaus asks Telemachus why he has come, and Telemachus tells of the suitors devouring his house and begs for any news of his father. Menelaus, indignant, likens the suitors to fawns laid in a lion's lair, wishes Odysseus were among them as he was when he threw Philomeleides at Lesbos, and promises to tell all that the Old Man of the Sea told him.

scenes.title: Eidothea's Counsel
scenes.summary: Becalmed for twenty days on Pharos off Egypt, his men starving, Menelaus meets Eidothea, daughter of Proteus, who tells him how to catch her father: at noon Proteus comes up out of the sea to sleep among his seals; Menelaus must hold him fast through all his changes until he speaks in his own shape.

scenes.title: The Capture of Proteus
scenes.summary: Eidothea hides Menelaus and three companions under fresh sealskins, with ambrosia to kill the smell. At midday Proteus counts his seals, counting the men among them, and lies down; they seize him, and he becomes a lion, a serpent, a leopard, a boar, water and a tree, until he grows weary and asks what they want. He tells Menelaus that he must sail back to the river Aegyptus and offer hecatombs before he can reach home.

scenes.title: Proteus' Tale of the Returns
scenes.summary: Proteus tells of the leaders who perished on the way home: Ajax, who boasted that he had escaped the sea against the gods' will and was drowned when Poseidon split the Gyraean rock, and Agamemnon, killed at a feast by Aegisthus; Odysseus is alive, held by Calypso on her island. Menelaus himself will not die in Argos: as Helen's husband and the son-in-law of Zeus he will be sent to the Elysian plain.

scenes.title: Menelaus' Return and His Gifts
scenes.summary: Menelaus sails back to Egypt, offers hecatombs, heaps up a tomb for Agamemnon and comes home. He asks Telemachus to stay eleven or twelve days and offers horses and a chariot; Telemachus must go, and asks for a gift he can carry, since Ithaca is a land for goats, not horses; Menelaus smiles and gives instead a mixing bowl of silver rimmed with gold, the work of Hephaestus. The banqueters come to the king's house.

scenes.title: The Suitors Learn of the Voyage
scenes.summary: In Ithaca the suitors are amusing themselves with discus and javelin when Noemon asks Antinous when Telemachus will be back with his ship. The suitors learn that the boy has really sailed, with Mentor or a god in Mentor's likeness; Antinous, his eyes like fire, asks for a ship and twenty men to ambush him in the strait between Ithaca and Samos.

scenes.title: Medon Tells Penelope
scenes.summary: The herald Medon, who has overheard the plot, tells Penelope. She rebukes the suitors for repaying with outrage a king who never wronged anyone, and when she hears that her son has gone to Pylos, speechlessness takes her; she asks why he had to go on the sea.

scenes.title: Penelope's Grief and Prayer
scenes.summary: Penelope sits on the threshold of her chamber and laments among her women that the storm winds have snatched away her son; she would send old Dolius to Laertes. Eurycleia confesses that she knew and swore to keep silent, and counsels her to pray to Athena. Penelope bathes, goes to her upper room, and prays to Athena with barley grains in a basket, raising the cry.

scenes.title: The Ambush Ship
scenes.summary: The suitors misread the cry as a sign of marriage. Antinous chooses twenty men, and they launch the ship, fit it out, and wait for evening. Penelope lies fasting in her upper room, pondering like a lion encircled by hunters, until sleep comes over her.

scenes.title: The Phantom of Iphthime
scenes.summary: Athena makes a phantom in the likeness of Penelope's sister Iphthime and sends it into her room. It tells her not to grieve, for Athena herself goes with her son; but when Penelope asks about Odysseus it will not say whether he lives, and slips away into the winds. Penelope wakes comforted by the clear dream.

scenes.title: The Ambush at Asteris
scenes.summary: The suitors sail out and lie in wait for Telemachus at Asteris, a small rocky island between Ithaca and Samos with a harbor open on either side.

days.label: Day 5
days.note: Lacedaemon: the arrival at nightfall, the wedding feast, the welcome, Helen's drug, the tales of Troy and the night in Menelaus' house (4.1–305), at the end of the day of the drive from Pherae (3.491–497).

days.label: Day 6
days.note: Menelaus' tale of Proteus and the gifts (4.306–619); the banqueters come to his house (4.620–624).

days.label: Day 4
days.note: Ithaca: Noemon saw Mentor there “yesterday at daybreak” (4.655–656), the morning after the ship sailed, so the suitors learn of the voyage on the fourth day, while Telemachus drives from Pylos to Pherae; that night Penelope dreams of her sister and the suitors sail out to lie in ambush (4.625–847). The poem tells the day in Ithaca after the day in Sparta.
